questions.stem:
It was only last month that Ravi’s Grandpa had come to live with them because he was getting too old to live on his own. It had been a difficult month with Grandpa having to be admitted to the hospital because he absent-mindedly took a double dose of his medicines, and then gave them several anxious moments when he got lost on one occasion he went for a walk and forgot the way back home.

Ravi's mother tells a neighbour that her father can no longer be left alone; which pair of events best explains her decision? (A) He fell in the garden at night and lay there until morning. (B) He took a double dose of his medicines and once lost his way home from a walk. (C) He was taken to hospital because he could not remember the way to his own flat. (D) He could not hear, see or remember well, and so could not run the household.

answerScheme.modelAnswer: He took a double dose of his medicines and once lost his way home from a walk.

questions.subject: English
questions.stem: Your grandfather has had to move in with your family because he is getting too old to live on his own, and he keeps reminding everyone that he has looked after himself for the better part of seventy-five years. Write a letter of about 100 words to him: tell him that the family wants him to stay, and suggest two things he could do at home that would make him feel useful.

markingPoints.description: Letter format: a correct salutation, the right addressee and a suitable closing
Content: shows respect for his self-reliance and explains why the family wants him to stay
Content: gives two specific jobs he can take over in the flat
Organisation: the ideas run in a clear order and the letter is split into short paragraphs
Accuracy and expression: correct spelling, punctuation and simple suitable language

answerScheme.modelAnswer:
Dear Grandfather,

Thank you for reading my letter. We all know you have looked after yourself for seventy-five years, and nobody wants to take that away from you.

Here is our plan for the flat. You will cook one dish a week, because you taught Mother her recipes and can now teach me. You will also keep the chess board and show me Karpov's opening against the computer, and tell me about the mistake Bobby Fischer made in his match with Spassky.

The walk to the corner shop is yours alone, and your chair, your tea and the Tamil paper will always be waiting.

With love,
Ravi

evidence: It was only last month that Ravi’s Grandpa had come to live with them because he was getting too old to live on his own.
I’ve been looking after myself for the better part of my seventy-five years.
That’s the opening move Karpov made when he played against the computer

questions.subject: English
questions.stem: At a meeting of your colony's residents a neighbour who has to look after her aged mother alone has asked you to speak on 'How neighbours can help elderly people who live by themselves'. Write a speech of about 100 words that gives two ways in which neighbours can help.

markingPoints.description: Speech format: a greeting to the audience and a closing of thanks
Content: explains why an elderly person living alone worries the speaker
Content: gives two clear, practical ways in which neighbours can help
Organisation: the two points are announced and developed one after the other
Accuracy and expression: correct spelling, punctuation and clear spoken language

answerScheme.modelAnswer:
Good evening, everyone.

My neighbour has looked after her aged mother alone for many months, and she worries every time her mother steps out. Let me suggest two ways in which we can help.

First, keep an eye out. An old person who goes for a walk may forget the way back, so a familiar face at the corner shop can bring her home safely.

Second, remove the dangers at home. A fall in the garden late in the evening can leave her lying outside all night.

If every family on this street took one small responsibility, no elderly person would face the day alone. Thank you.

evidence: and then gave them several anxious moments when he got lost on one occasion he went for a walk and forgot the way back home.
Grandpa had slipped and fallen in the garden late one evening while he was pottering around and lain outside all night because there was no one at home to help him up.

After your mother died ten years ago, I took over her duties as well and have been cooking, shopping and keeping house too.

A classmate asks what the mention of the old man's job as a lawyer tells us about the way he speaks; which answer is correct? (A) It shows that he had given up the practice of law before he spoke to his daughter. (B) It shows that his daughter had been trained in the same profession. (C) It shows that the harshness in his voice came from anger and not from his training. (D) It shows that the firmness in his voice was natural to a man whose job was as a lawyer.

answerScheme.modelAnswer: It shows that the firmness in his voice was natural to a man whose job was as a lawyer.

questions.stem: Ravi follows his grandfather across the city without being seen, and every stop brings a fresh crisis for him. Write the stops in order and, against each one, note what happens to Ravi.

markingPoints.description: Children's park: he crouches behind an elephant-shaped bush, is accused of shooing a child and crawls out on all fours
Tea stall: he hides behind a banyan tree, the vendors accuse him of talking loudly, and he ducks behind a silver car
Barber shop: his grandfather goes in and Ravi crosses the road and ducks into the shop next door
The next door shop is a Ladies' Hairdressing Salon and he is evicted amidst a volley of feminine shrieks
Bus stop: his grandfather boards the first bus and Ravi jumps on seconds before it starts
He pushes to the front of the bus and finds a total stranger wearing his grandfather's cap

answerScheme.modelAnswer:

2. The boy's mother accuses him of shooing her child and threatens him with an umbrella, and he crawls out on all fours.
3. Tea stall - he hides behind a big banyan tree, and the vendors accuse him of talking loudly.
4. They surround him, so he concedes defeat and ducks behind a shiny silver car.

6. Bus stop - his grandfather boards the first bus; Ravi jumps on seconds before it starts and finds a total stranger in the yellow cap.

questions.subject: English
questions.stem: Ravi pushes his way to the front of the bus to confront the man in the yellow cap and finds a total stranger. Show in steps how Ravi is led to this mistake and how it is explained away, and say what the explanation tells you about his grandfather.

markingPoints.description: Ravi's suspicion begins with the full head of grey hair revealed when the cap comes off in the warm bus
He pushes to the front of the bus expecting to confront his grandfather, but finds a total stranger
The stranger wears a white pyjama and shirt, his grandfather's standard attire, and a cap with a coffee-stain on its rim
The stranger says a kind old gentleman in the barber shop made him take the cap because it was a hot day
The writer calls this typical of the grandfather, who is always generous
Ravi has still not found his grandfather, leaving his whereabouts unanswered

answerScheme.modelAnswer:
1. On the warm bus the cap comes off and a full head of grey hair appears; Ravi even wonders whether his grandfather has bought a wig.
2. He pushes to the front of the bus expecting to confront his grandfather.
3. He finds a total stranger in a white pyjama and shirt, his grandfather's standard attire, and a yellow cap with a coffee-stain on its rim just like his grandfather's.
4. The stranger says a kind old gentleman in the barber shop insisted that he take the cap because it was such a hot day.
5. The writer calls this typical of his grandfather, always generous, so the mix-up closes warmly.
6. Ravi has still not found his grandfather, and where the old man has gone is left unanswered.

evidence: It was warm inside the bus so Grandpa took off his cap to reveal … a full head of grey hair! Ravi was startled.
He was wearing a white pyjama and shirt, which was Grandpa’s standard attire, and a yellow cap exactly like Grandpa’s.
a kind old gentleman in the barber shop had insisted that he take his cap because it was such a hot day. That was typical of Grandpa, always generous.
